with:</p> <p>* QuickBooks<br>* Microsoft Excel — advanced level<br>* Financial data reconciliation<br>* Data analysis and reporting<br>* Purchase orders and vendor bills<br>* Accounts payable and/or We embed with our clients, join their standups, and stay with their product as it evolves. Average client retention is 24+ months, which means you'll see what your work does to a business over years, not weeks.</p> <p>We're looking for a <strong>Senior Visual Designer</strong> to own client work from concept through final delivery. This is not a role where you execute someone else's brief. You'll understand the business strategy behind each project, identify the user experience problems our client's customers have been stuck on, and use design to solve them.</p> <p>You'll work directly with our leadership, our client's leadership, our design leads and you'll direct specialists in motion, and illustration on your projects.</p> <h2>Qualifications</h2> <ul> <li>7+ years designing digital products (ideally with an agency)</li> <li>Strong fundamentals: <ul> <li>Excellence in communication (can communicate with a team and various stakeholders)</li> <li>Excellence in aesthetic (UI/Visual design)</li> <li>Excellence in craft (Figma Hygiene, design principles and delight)</li> <li>Excellence in strategy (Can interpret vague requirements and clarify them + can drive product change through compelling concepts, prototypes and mockups)</li> </ul> </li> <li>Expert-level Figma. Comfort with prototyping (AI or traditional tools) and motion is a strong plus</li> <li>Ability to effectively prioritize tasks and delegate work to a teammate (production designer)</li> <li>Confident communicator who can present and defend work directly to senior clients and founders. Our clients are opinionated and educated about design, it's not your typical agency! You will need to defend great design less vigorously but it will be expected more often.</li> <li>Comfortable with ambiguity and able to move fast without dropping quality</li> <li>Self-driven and organized enough to run your own project workflows without being managed</li> </ul> <h2>Responsibilities</h2> <ul> <li>Produce design work at a consistently high quality tier, with meticulous attention to craft, precision, and completeness.</li> <li>Define the design challenge at a strategic level, connecting solutions to client goals, strategy, and business vision. Identify the historical positioning problems behind each brief and design with those in mind</li> <li>Build and maintain style kits that give the team and collaborators a clear, consistent visual language</li> <li>Brief and coordinate specialists: translate client requirements into actionable direction for production designers, illustrators, motion designers, 3d artists and give feedback that keeps output aligned with the creative vision</li> <li>Communicate proactively with clients: estimate effort and timelines accurately, respond to Slack within one business hour during working hours.</li> <li>Own projects end to end, from brief through final delivery</li> <li>Maintain asset hygiene: files clean, structured, and aligned with team fundamentals</li> <li>Manage project operations in Notion, keeping planning pages, task boards, and meeting notes current without being prompted</li> <li>Prioritize effectively, focusing on the right tasks in the right order at the right time</li> <li>Participate actively in team rituals: crits, elevate sessions, and growth activities</li> </ul> <h2>Highlights</h2> <p> <strong>Meaningful work:</strong> Partner directly with founders and executives at companies building serious products. Your designs ship to real users and move real businesses. Our clients come back after they exit. We develop deep relationship with them which means we're able to see the impact of our work overtime (unheard of in a traditional agency).</p> <p><strong> Exceptional team:</strong> Work alongside designers who are generous collaborators, not competitors. Everyone here is deeply skilled and genuinely invested in lifting the team up.</p> <p><strong> Remote:</strong> We're distributed (mostly across Canada) and flexible about where you work, as long as you cover PT and ET hours with stellar internet.</p> <p> <strong>Offsites:</strong> We meet in person at least 2 times per year! Past locations: Montreal, Toronto, Barcelona, Greece, Miami, &nbsp;Mont-Tremblant, &nbsp;Tulum</p> <p> <strong>Growth investment:</strong> We cover courses, workshops, and other learning you want to pursue. We also run weekly elevate sessions where the team sharpens design and thinking skills together.</p> <p> <strong>Cross-disciplinary collaboration:</strong> Work with motion designers, illustrators, and other specialists. We embed with our clients, join their standups, and stay with their product as it evolves. Average client retention is 24+ months, which means you'll see what your work does to a business over years, not weeks.</p> <p>We're looking for a <strong>Senior Visual Designer</strong> to own client work from concept through final delivery. This is not a role where you execute someone else's brief. You'll understand the business strategy behind each project, identify the user experience problems our client's customers have been stuck on, and use design to solve them.</p> <p>You'll work directly with our leadership, our client's leadership, our design leads and you'll direct specialists in motion, and illustration on your projects.</p> <h2>Qualifications</h2> <ul> <li>7+ years designing digital products (ideally with an agency)</li> <li>Strong fundamentals: <ul> <li>Excellence in communication (can communicate with a team and various stakeholders)</li> <li>Excellence in aesthetic (UI/Visual design)</li> <li>Excellence in craft (Figma Hygiene, design principles and delight)</li> <li>Excellence in strategy (Can interpret vague requirements and clarify them + can drive product change through compelling concepts, prototypes and mockups)</li> </ul> </li> <li>Expert-level Figma. Comfort with prototyping (AI or traditional tools) and motion is a strong plus</li> <li>Ability to effectively prioritize tasks and delegate work to a teammate (production designer)</li> <li>Confident communicator who can present and defend work directly to senior clients and founders. Our clients are opinionated and educated about design, it's not your typical agency! You will need to defend great design less vigorously but it will be expected more often.</li> <li>Comfortable with ambiguity and able to move fast without dropping quality</li> <li>Self-driven and organized enough to run your own project workflows without being managed</li> </ul> <h2>Responsibilities</h2> <ul> <li>Produce design work at a consistently high quality tier, with meticulous attention to craft, precision, and completeness.</li> <li>Define the design challenge at a strategic level, connecting solutions to client goals, strategy, and business vision. Identify the historical positioning problems behind each brief and design with those in mind</li> <li>Build and maintain style kits that give the team and collaborators a clear, consistent visual language</li> <li>Brief and coordinate specialists: translate client requirements into actionable direction for production designers, illustrators, motion designers, 3d artists and give feedback that keeps output aligned with the creative vision</li> <li>Communicate proactively with clients: estimate effort and timelines accurately, respond to Slack within one business hour during working hours.</li> <li>Own projects end to end, from brief through final delivery</li> <li>Maintain asset hygiene: files clean, structured, and aligned with team fundamentals</li> <li>Manage project operations in Notion, keeping planning pages, task boards, and meeting notes current without being prompted</li> <li>Prioritize effectively, focusing on the right tasks in the right order at the right time</li> <li>Participate actively in team rituals: crits, elevate sessions, and growth activities</li> </ul> <h2>Highlights</h2> <p> <strong>Meaningful work:</strong> Partner directly with founders and executives at companies building serious products. Your designs ship to real users and move real businesses. Our clients come back after they exit. We develop deep relationship with them which means we're able to see the impact of our work overtime (unheard of in a traditional agency).</p> <p><strong> Exceptional team:</strong> Work alongside designers who are generous collaborators, not competitors. Everyone here is deeply skilled and genuinely invested in lifting the team up.</p> <p><strong> Remote:</strong> We're distributed (mostly across Canada) and flexible about where you work, as long as you cover PT and ET hours with stellar internet.</p> <p> <strong>Offsites:</strong> We meet in person at least 2 times per year! These are good moments to get the team together, celebrate our accomplishments and align on a unified vision. Past locations: Montreal, Toronto, Barcelona, Greece, Miami, &nbsp;Mont-Tremblant, &nbsp;Tulum</p> <p> <strong>Growth investment:</strong> We cover courses, workshops, and other learning you want to pursue. Just bring it to your manager. We also run weekly elevate sessions where the team sharpens design and thinking skills together.</p> <p> <strong>Cross-disciplinary collaboration:</strong> Work with motion designers, illustrators, and other specialists. You'll expand your craft and find more opportunities for delight.</p> <p>️ <strong>Clarity:</strong> You'll know what's expected of you, what you need to succeed in the role, and how to grow beyond it.</p> <p><strong>⛑️ Health insurance:</strong> All Canada based employees receive private health insurance.</p> <h2>How to Apply</h2> <p>All applications will be reviewed through our recruiting system, and we'll reach out to selected candidates with the next steps.</p> <p> Please submit your application using our <a href="https://app.notion.com/p/fcad48e86e1183e8ad8381b02c56eb1a?pvs=21">application form</a>.</p> <p><strong>To apply:</strong> <a href="https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/pixel-one-senior-visual-designer">https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/pixel-one-senior-visual-designer</a></p> Tue, 11 Aug 2026 03:24:55 +0000 Thu, 10 Sep 2026 03:24:55 +0000 https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/pixel-one-senior-visual-designer https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/pixel-one-senior-visual-designer Pixel One: Senior Product Designer Anywhere in the World Florida Figma Design Full-Time <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Canada <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://pixel-one.com/">https://pixel-one.com/</a> </p> <p><em>Full-time · Remote (Canada based preferred)</em></p> <p>Pixel One is a design studio for ambitious B2B SaaS teams. newContent: We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more en-US 60 Justworks: International Consultant, APAC Anywhere in the World All Other Remote Full-Time <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote - International </p> <div class="content-intro"><h1><strong>Who We Are</strong></h1> <p><span>At Justworks, you’ll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people.</span></p> <p><span>We’re helping businesses get off the ground by enabling them to focus on running their business. We solve HR issues. We’re data-driven and never stop iterating. If you’d like to work in a supportive, entrepreneurial environment, are interested in building something meaningful and having fun while doing it, we’d love to hear from you.</span></p> <p><span>We're united by shared goals and shared motivations at Justworks. These are best summed up in our company values, which are reflected in our product and in our team.</span></p> <p><a href="https://www.justworks.com/careers#values"><span>Our Values</span></a></p> <p><span>If this sounds like you, you’ll fit right in.</span></p></div><h1><strong>Who You Are</strong></h1> <p>You are a strategic advisor and a jurisdictional expert with a proven track record of helping global customers navigate high-stakes complexities in the APAC region. You are consultative, proactive, and passionate about turning nuanced challenges into actionable solutions. You are comfortable solving open-ended, high-risk problems and serving as the final authority on complex APAC employment and Employer of Record (EOR) practices. You build trust easily, collaborate across teams, and advocate for customers while strategically mitigating risk for the business.</p> <p>As an International Consultant, you are the subject matter expert and trusted advisor for Justworks’ international customers. While the Support Specialist team handles tactical platform navigation and payroll inquiries, you focus on the complex moments—including jurisdictional separation guidance, international benefits strategy, and global regulatory compliance in the APAC region. You own the strategic relationship for customers expanding into diverse international markets, ensuring they maximize the value of Justworks' global offerings while maintaining total compliance.</p> <h1><strong>Your Success Profile</strong></h1> <p><strong>What You Will Work On</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as a definitive subject matter expert for EOR services across diverse APAC markets, maintaining deep knowledge of varying regulatory environments.</li> <li>Act as the primary advisor for complex APAC compliance requirements, providing strategic recommendations on cross-border employment nuances, terminations, and local labor standards to mitigate global risk.</li> <li>Partner with Legal, Product, and Operations to interpret global industry trends and regulatory shifts, directly influencing international product-market fit and go-to-market strategies.</li> <li>Partner with Customer Success to manage high-value accounts, addressing sophisticated, territory-specific needs that require advanced jurisdictional expertise.</li> <li>Act as the final point of internal escalation for inquiries that cross into complex compliance or high-liability HR territory, such as intricate leave scenarios and country-specific benefits.</li> <li>Proactively identify EOR expansion and upsell opportunities, guiding customers through the strategic complexities of entering and scaling in new international markets.</li> <li>Drive retention and growth of existing customer base through an education-based approach.&nbsp;</li> <li>Translate complex international regulations and processes into clear, actionable guidance for customers and internal partners.</li> <li>Operate independently while contributing to team knowledge and scaling best practices across the organization.</li> <li>Utilize deep global knowledge to advise customers on legally sensitive and region-specific paths forward.</li> <li>Serve as the voice of the specialized customer to ensure Justworks’ international infrastructure meets the needs of complex, multinational organizations.</li> <li>Other duties as needed based on departmental/organizational needs.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>How You Will Do Your Work</strong></h2> <p>As an International Consultant, how results are achieved is paramount for your success and ultimately result in our success as an organization. In this role, your foundational knowledge, skills, abilities and personal attributes are anchored in the following competencies:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Consultative - </strong>Takes an approach that focuses on building relationships with others, understanding their problems, and developing solutions to their challenges through open-ended questions and active listening.</li> <li><strong>Taking responsibility - </strong>Being accountable, being committed, and accepting ownership for one's decisions, actions, and behavior.</li> <li><strong>Adaptability - </strong>The ability to adjust your approach or actions in response to changes in your internal and external environment.</li> <li><strong>Solution-oriented - </strong>Identifies the source of a question or challenge and provides the right, or a better, way of doing things.</li> <li><strong>Curious - </strong>The innate desire to learn, grow and understand.</li> </ul> <p>In addition, all Justworkers focus on aligning their behaviors to our core values known as COGIS. It stands for:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Camaraderie</strong> - Day to day you can be seen working together toward a higher purpose. You like to have fun. You’re an active listener, treat people respectfully, and have a strong desire to know and help others.</li> <li><strong>Openness</strong> - Your default is to be open. You're willing to share information, understand other perspectives, and consider new possibilities. You’re curious, ask open questions, and are receptive to thoughts and feedback from others.</li> <li><strong>Grit </strong>- You demonstrate grit by having the courage to commit and persevere. You’re committed, earnest, and dive in to get the job done well with a positive attitude.</li> <li><strong>Integrity</strong> - Simply put, do what you say and say what you'll do. You’re honest and forthright, have a strong moral compass, and strive to match your words with your actions while leading by example.&nbsp;</li> <li><strong>Simplicity</strong> - Be like Einstein: “Everything should be made as simple as possible, but no simpler.”</li> </ul> <p><strong>Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>8+ years of experience in a customer-facing international HR role, ideally with deep expertise in APAC and the EOR space.</li> <li>Proven track record of managing strategic conversations and complex global customer HR scenarios with minimum of 2 years managing complex customer-facing issues in EOR.</l

oldContent: Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ Data-driven reporting on private markets, startups, founders, and investors Mon, 10 Aug 2026 00:50:32 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=6.8.7 https://news.crunchbase.com/wp-content/uploads/cb_news_favicon-150x150.png Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ 32 32 Global New Unicorn Counts In The First Half Of 2026 Have Already Surpassed 2025’s Totals https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/global-unicorn-counts-rise-ai-robotics-chips-h1-2026/ Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:00:38 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=93956 A total 195 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in the first half of 2026 — far surpassing counts seen since the second half of 2022. Already, H1 is above the new unicorn totals for all of 2025, when 193 companies were minted with that status. In this bifurcated funding environment, we also see a wide range in valuations, as well as select companies that raised multiple rounds at a significant valuation increase in the space of months. Among this cohort, robotics and AI neolabs were the leading sectors for new unicorns. Other industries that stand out were in financial services, healthcare and biotech as well as AI infrastructure, AI deployment and devtools, defense, semiconductor and aerospace. H1 new unicorns have added roughly $440 billion in value to the board — 5% of the board’s current value. These companies have raised $80 billion over time, representing 5% of funding raised by still-private, unicorn-valued companies. The most valuable new unicorn this year is China-based open-source model developer DeepSeek , which was valued at $50 billion in its first external financing. Seychelles-based crypto exchange OKX , valued at $25 billion, is the second most valuable company to join in the first half of this year. San Francisco-based OpenAI Deployment Co. , majority owned by OpenAI and valued at $14 billion when it raised $4 billion from private equity, is in the third spot. From this cohort, four companies were valued as decacorns in H1, and a further five were valued above $5 billion, as of early August 2026. Based on trends for 2025 companies, we expect valuations for this cohort to climb significantly in the next year. For the 193 new unicorns that joined in 2025, 12 were decacorns and another 18 were valued above $5 billion. Nine of those decacorns for this cohort became $10 billion-plus-valued companies in 2026. US leads, China picks up The U.S. leads with 110 companies — 56% of new unicorns in H1. China was in second place with 38 companies, a significant surge from 10 new unicorns in 2025. The U.K. was the third-largest market with 13 companies joining. By continent, North America accounts for 115 new unicorns, Asia with 50 and Europe with 27. Latin America, Oceania and Africa each count for one. Fast raises In the current frenzied funding environment, 19 of H1’s new unicorns raised fast follow-on rounds, often in six months or less, and doubled on an earlier valuation to reach at least $2 billion or more. Notable among the fast fundraisers are semiconductor startup Etched , which doubled its prior valuation to $10 billion from $5 billion just six months earlier; defense tech unicorn Hadrian , whose valuation vaulted to $7.9 billion, up from its prior $1.6 billion valuation seven months earlier; and Valar Atomics , building nuclear energy reactors for AI, was valued at $6 billion, up from $2 billion four months earlier. AI momentum Trillions in value were added to The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in the first half of the year, including from some of the largest-ever venture funding deals. The first six months of 2026 also notched the largest venture-backed exit of all time: SpaceX ’s IPO. Taken together with the rapid follow-on raises at ever-larger valuations some of those companies have achieved, it’s clear that the momentum around the fastest-growing companies has picked up significantly in this AI cycle. It’s What Happens Afterward. https://news.crunchbase.com/public/ai-ipo-results-lp-liquidity-gershfeld-flint/ Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:00:36 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=93952 By Andrew Gershfeld The current focus on AI IPOs is largely centered on public market performance. Investors want to know whether these companies justify their valuations and how their shares will trade after listing. But everybody is watching the wrong metric. The more consequential story begins after the bell rings, when limited partners receive distributions and decide where to deploy that capital next. At sufficient scale, AI IPOs become a capital formation event for the broader venture ecosystem. If several of the largest AI companies reach the public markets over the next few years, those exits could reshape venture fundraising and further concentrate capital among the industry’s largest firms. The real story begins after the IPO Andrew Gershfeld, general partner at Flint Capital. The more meaningful process starts when investors receive distributions from successful exits. Pension funds, university endowments, sovereign wealth funds and family offices rarely leave that capital sitting idle for long. As portfolios are rebalanced, investment committees begin evaluating new commitments across private markets. Venture has spent several years waiting for meaningful liquidity. Higher private valuations may improve paper returns, but they do not return capital to limited partners. Only successful exits complete that cycle. SpaceX ’s $85.7 billion IPO illustrates both the potential and the limits of a single listing. One IPO alone is unlikely to transform venture fundraising. But a sustained wave of listings involving companies such as OpenAI , Anthropic , Databricks and Stripe could steadily return capital to investors and give limited partners
newContent: Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ Data-driven reporting on private markets, startups, founders, and investors Mon, 10 Aug 2026 17:40:57 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=6.8.7 https://news.crunchbase.com/wp-content/uploads/cb_news_favicon-150x150.png Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ 32 32 The VC Firm That Helped Build Latin America’s Startup Scene Is Crossing Into Silicon Valley https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/latam-startup-vc-silicon-valley-expansion-qa-quinzanos-monashees/ Tue, 11 Aug 2026 11:00:59 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=93965 Monashees , one of Latin America’s oldest and most influential VC firms, believes the next phase of the region’s startup ecosystem requires a permanent Silicon Valley presence. The firm, which was founded more than two decades ago in São Paulo, last year opened a San Francisco office to connect LatAm’s startup entrepreneurs with the money and AI research coursing through the Bay Area. Fabiola Quinzaños, a partner in Monashees Silicon Valley office. (Courtesy photo) We spoke with Fabiola Quinzaños to talk through the firm’s evolution and how it is meeting this AI moment. She is a partner at the firm who relocated to Silicon Valley from Mexico City. When the firm was founded in 2005, Brazil didn’t yet have a startup ecosystem — there was no network of founders, no LPs backing VC firms based there, and no follow-on investors. That has changed drastically in the couple of decades since, with the country emerging as LatAm’s startup powerhouse and a place where U.S. investors and tech giants are increasingly courting business. Brazil is an exceptionally digitally savvy market. It is the highest-volume market for Uber and the third-largest by visitor share for ChatGPT . Its real-time payment rail Pix , created by the Central Bank of Brazil , was rolled out in 2020 and is used by more than 90% of adults in the country. Latin America has also become an important market for U.S. AI labs and technology companies. Monashees recently announced a partnership with Google called the Gama Fund in which the two companies co-invest up to $2 million in AI-native and deep tech pre-seed or seed-stage startups in Brazil. Its first summit is planned for later this year in San Francisco, where it will gather Latin American startup founders building businesses with AI. Monashees makes around eight to 10 new investments per year and is finalizing the deployment of its $370 million fund into roughly 35 companies. The firm opened an office in Mexico City in 2022 and in September 2025 set up an office in San Francisco. The interview has been edited for brevity and clarity. Gené Teare: To set this up, tell me about Monashees. Fabiola Quinzaños: Monashees is the pioneer of venture capital in Latin America. It started 20 years ago, in 2005, with the premise that what had happened in Silicon Valley with tech could also happen in LatAm — that many of the structural problems could be solved with tech. Eric Acher and Fabio Igel , Monashees’ co-founders, were crazy enough to believe this could happen, so that’s when they started Monashees. Just to give you a little context, back in the day there was nothing. It really took time for this flywheel to get started, because if you don’t have funding, you don’t have great talent. Finally, after five years, they managed to crack that. In 2010, you started to have the first wave of tech companies in the region, and Monashees started positioning Brazil on the global tech map. As a second phase, the team realized that what was happening in the Brazilian ecosystem was also starting to happen in other countries in the region. Great teams were starting to build great companies. That’s when Monashees decided to expand across Latin America and back these teams. That’s when we led Rappi ’s seed round, one of the flagship companies of Latin America. The third wave, which is what we’re focused on right now, is Global LatAm: backing Latin American founders who are building global businesses, regardless of whether they are building in Latin America or globally. That has also been the rationale for opening an office in San Francisco. In the context of AI, you have many Latin American founders starting businesses from here because you have to be close to the labs and the talent. We’re early-stage investors. We invest at pre-seed, seed and Series A. Seed and Series A are our sweet spot, and we are lead investors. We’re also generalists. We’re not sector-specific, we’re mostly sector-agnostic. I see this trend when I talk to a lot of European VCs with earlier-stage investors, establishing a U.S. presence. It seems fairly recent, and it seems to be driven by this AI wave. Do you think it’s the VCs coming here and the founders following, or are the founders coming first and the VCs realizing they need more of a presence here? Quinzaños: I think initially it was mostly founders. Now, it’s a little bit of both; they’re feeding each other. The reason we started the office in San Francisco is that the pace at which AI evolves is unseen, even compared with other technology paradigms in the past. If you’re not here, it’s very difficult to keep pace and stay up to speed with where the AI frontier is going. You even have a gap with Wall Street, so imagine the gap with Latin America. If you want to build an AI-native company as a Latin American founder, part of that is coming to San Francisco and Silicon Valley. San Francisco is now the magnet for all of this. It’s highly dense and concentrated. You have to be here to absorb the tools and understand what other people are doing. I also think it’s super important because founders realize that Silicon Valley is the champions league. In Latin America, you do have great talent, but you don’t know what great looks like if you’ve never worked here. The reason we opened an office here is to bridge that gap: to help founders be here, see what is happening at the frontier, and understand what the best companies are doing so they can replicate that back in LatAm. The talent in the region is now sophisticated enough. It has been a 20-year process to get to a point where you have great, ambitious founders who believe they can build global businesses. You already have success stories like Vercel from Guillermo Rauch or Kalshi from Luana Lopes Lara . Founders realize they can build globally. In the context of AI, many of these global companies have to be based here because you have access to AI talent, but also to funding. Being close to all the Silicon Valley funds is also crucial for them. I do think several founders are coming here to build, but that also creates some issues. One important thing to note is that many of these founders are building for the Latin American market, where your revenue is in Brazilian reais or Mexican pesos. In terms of headcount, you need to be very careful that you don’t have a U.S. cost basis when your revenue is in Brazilian reais or Mexican pesos. These very early-stage startups also cannot compete with the big labs here that are paying a lot of money for talent. Right now in San Francisco, finding AI talent is really difficult and it’s very expensive. I think it’s more about coming here, learning and bringing back the best practices. That’s where the real arbitrage opportunity comes from. You have amazing talent in LatAm, and you can teach them. Now, in the context of AI, you have much better ways to do that and you can operate with a smaller headcount. That’s the rationale for founders coming here and for us being here as a bridge. We help our portfolio companies stay close to AI innovation, but we also get access to Latin American founders who are building from the U.S. We hired a researcher for the Monashees team. oldContent: We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more en-US 60 Justworks: International Consultant, APAC Anywhere in the World All Other Remote Full-Time <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote - International </p> <div class="content-intro"><h1><strong>Who We Are</strong></h1> <p><span>At Justworks, you’ll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people.</span></p> <p><span>We’re helping businesses get off the ground by enabling them to focus on running their business. We solve HR issues. We’re data-driven and never stop iterating. If you’d like to work in a supportive, entrepreneurial environment, are interested in building something meaningful and having fun while doing it, we’d love to hear from you.</span></p> <p><span>We're united by shared goals and shared motivations at Justworks. These are best summed up in our company values, which are reflected in our product and in our team.</span></p> <p><a href="https://www.justworks.com/careers#values"><span>Our Values</span></a></p> <p><span>If this sounds like you, you’ll fit right in.</span></p></div><h1><strong>Who You Are</strong></h1> <p>You are a strategic advisor and a jurisdictional expert with a proven track record of helping global customers navigate high-stakes complexities in the APAC region. You are consultative, proactive, and passionate about turning nuanced challenges into actionable solutions. You are comfortable solving open-ended, high-risk problems and serving as the final authority on complex APAC employment and Employer of Record (EOR) practices. You build trust easily, collaborate across teams, and advocate for customers while strategically mitigating risk for the business.</p> <p>As an International Consultant, you are the subject matter expert and trusted advisor for Justworks’ international customers. While the Support Specialist team handles tactical platform navigation and payroll inquiries, you focus on the complex moments—including jurisdictional separation guidance, international benefits strategy, and global regulatory compliance in the APAC region. You own the strategic relationship for customers expanding into diverse international markets, ensuring they maximize the value of Justworks' global offerings while maintaining total compliance.</p> <h1><strong>Your Success Profile</strong></h1> <p><strong>What You Will Work On</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as a definitive subject matter expert for EOR services across diverse APAC markets, maintaining deep knowledge of varying regulatory environments.</li> <li>Act as the primary advisor for complex APAC compliance requirements, providing strategic recommendations on cross-border employment nuances, terminations, and local labor standards to mitigate global risk.</li> <li>Partner with Legal, Product, and Operations to interpret global industry trends and regulatory shifts, directly influencing international product-market fit and go-to-market strategies.</li> <li>Partner with Customer Success to manage high-value accounts, addressing sophisticated, territory-specific needs that require advanced jurisdictional expertise.</li> <li>Act as the final point of internal escalation for inquiries that cross into complex compliance or high-liability HR territory, such as intricate leave scenarios and country-specific benefits.</li> <li>Proactively identify EOR expansion and upsell opportunities, guiding customers through the strategic complexities of entering and scaling in new international markets.</li> <li>Drive retention and growth of existing customer base through an education-based approach.&nbsp;</li> <li>Translate complex international regulations and processes into clear, actionable guidance for customers and internal partners.</li> <li>Operate independently while contributing to team knowledge and scaling best practices across the
